stories.title: Selldorf Architects Signs Long-Term Renewal at 860 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Colliers SVP Seth Hecht has secured a 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease renewal for architecture firm Selldorf Architects at 860 Broadway. Hecht represented Gordon Property Group in completing the long-term renewal transaction. Selldorf Architects was represented by Erik Schmall and Scott Weiss of Savills. Led by internationally acclaimed architect Annabelle Selldorf, the firm has called 860 Broadway home for the past two decades. “860 Broadway is one of Manhattan’s iconic office buildings, and its location continues to make it a highly desirable destination for creative and innovative companies,” said Hecht. “When a firm as globally respected as Selldorf Architects commits to another decade in the building, it speaks to both the property’s enduring appeal and the long-term strength of this market.” In addition to Selldorf Architects, current 860 Broadway tenants include Industrious, Valon and retail tenant Uniqlo. Hecht is also representing Gordon Property Group in leasing three additional Manhattan office properties. The post Selldorf Architects Signs Long-Term Renewal at 860 Broadway appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Selldorf Architects renews 13,815 SF at 860 Broadway, Manhattan for 10 years
Firm anchors creative office sector in Flatiron District after 20-year tenure
Gordon Property Group retains high-quality tenant; market signals strong creative-office demand
stories.summary: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects has renewed its 10-year lease for 13,815 square feet at 860 Broadway in the Flatiron District, where it has been located for two decades. Colliers represented landlord Gordon Property Group; Savills represented the tenant. The renewal reflects sustained demand for creative office space in Midtown South, where Class A asking rents averaged $97.22/SF in Q2.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact to multifamily development. Office tenant retention in Manhattan signals resilience in creative-sector employment but does not materially affect residential demand, supply, or capital allocation for apartment projects.

stories.title: Innocean USA Signs 100K-SF lease with Hackman Capital in Headquarters Relocation
stories.excerpt: Advertising agency Innocean USA has signed a new 101,000-square-foot office lease at Hackman Capital Partners’ 888 N. Douglas property in El Segundo. The space will serve as the company’s U.S. headquarters and represents a relocation from 50,000 square feet of space in Huntington Beach. The tenant will move into its new space after construction concludes in 2027. JLL’s Jason Fine, Jeff Ingham, and Mitch Lundquist represented INNOCEAN USA in the new lease. Hackman Capital represented itself. “This is a transformative change for INNOCEAN USA, and we spent years advising the leadership team to help find a ‘one of one’ facility that would bring their company vision of the future to reality,” said Fine. “This is going to be a special place where their employees and creativity will absolutely thrive.” Across from the Lakers’ practice facility and the L.A. Times headquarters, 888 Douglas is a 30-acre campus with four buildings totaling approximately 550,000 square feet. Hackman Capital purchased the 1930s-era aerospace manufacturing site in 2016 and invested $100 million to transform it into a creative office campus. The post Innocean USA Signs 100K-SF lease with Hackman Capital in Headquarters Relocation appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Innocean USA relocates HQ from Huntington Beach to El Segundo; 101K SF lease, 2027 delivery
~600 employee relocation signals job/population concentration shift in South Los Angeles metro
Hackman's $100M creative campus investment (888 Douglas) attracts major tenant doubling footprint
stories.summary: Advertising agency Innocean USA signed a 101,000-square-foot headquarters lease at Hackman Capital Partners' 888 Douglas campus in El Segundo, relocating nearly 600 employees from 50,000 SF in Huntington Beach. The company will occupy the space after construction completes in 2027. Hackman acquired the former aerospace manufacturing site in 2016 and invested $100 million transforming it into a 550,000-SF creative office campus.
stories.impact: Significant signal for South Los Angeles (El Segundo/LAX-adjacent submarket) rental demand: a 600-person white-collar employer migration from Orange County into the metro area signals job-growth inflow and potential residential demand surge in adjacent multifamily markets (Manhattan Beach, Hermosa Beach, Torrance, Inglewood). Track residential absorption and rent growth in a 5-10 mile radius of 888 Douglas over 2027–2028; this precedent may attract follow-on corporate relocations to the campus and drive rental demand.

stories.title: MADDD Equities Scoops Up Vacant West Farms Industrial
stories.excerpt: Ariel Property Advisors closed the sale of 425 Devoe Ave., a vacant multi-story industrial property in the West Farms neighborhood of The Bronx, for $10,750,000. The property spans 60,000 square feet above grade, which translates to $180 per square foot, with an additional 30,000 square feet below grade. An Ariel investment sales team led by senior director Jason M. Gold, along with partner Sean R. Kelly, Esq. and director Daniel Mahfa represented the seller, Abingdon Square Partners. The buyer was MADDD Equities, LLC. “The sale of 425 Devoe Ave. demonstrates the strong demand for large, commercial sites offering convenient regional access,” said Gold. Situated on a 40,097-square-foot lot, the property features four levels of usable industrial and warehouse space. It is located near the 2 and 5 subway lines and offers convenient access to the Cross Bronx Expressway, Sheridan Boulevard and the broader New York region. The post MADDD Equities Scoops Up Vacant West Farms Industrial appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MADDD Equities acquires 425 Devoe Ave., West Farms Bronx for $10.75M; 60K SF above-grade industrial
Property trades at $180/SF; 30K SF below-grade; proximate to 2/5 subway, Cross Bronx Expressway
Strong demand for large industrial sites with regional transit access drives acquisition by institutional buyer
stories.summary: Ariel Property Advisors closed the sale of 425 Devoe Avenue, a vacant 60,000-square-foot above-grade industrial property in West Farms, Bronx, to MADDD Equities for $10.75 million ($180/SF). The four-story industrial asset sits on a 40,097-SF lot with convenient access to the 2 and 5 subway lines, Cross Bronx Expressway, and regional highways. An additional 30,000 SF below grade is included.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance; however, the $180/SF valuation and strong institutional demand for large industrial sites with transit/highway access in the Bronx may signal opportunity for value-add industrial-to-residential conversion or mixed-use redevelopment in West Farms and adjacent neighborhoods. Monitor zoning flexibility and conversion feasibility in Bronx industrial corridors, which could unlock residential supply in transit-rich submarkets with historically lower land and construction costs.

stories.title: Shopoff Secures Approval for Buena Park Residential Development
stories.excerpt: Shopoff Realty Investments has secured unanimous approval from the Buena Park City Council for 5600 Beach Blvd, a 13.76-acre residential development in Buena Park. The property is currently occupied by the Amway Corporation with a corporate sale-leaseback in place until the end of 2026 and consists of two industrial buildings totaling approximately 370,031 square feet. “5600 Beach Blvd represents an important step forward for Orange County and is intended to help address the need for attainable and diverse housing options for first-time homebuyers and for Buena Park’s growing senior population,” said Shopoff Realty Investments’ president and CEO, Bill Shopoff. “Transforming an industrial site into a vibrant residential community aligns with the city and county’s evolving needs, providing homes for people at every stage of life.” The development aims to deliver 231 three-story townhomes and duplex units, offered with four different floor plans, along with 50 for-rent senior affordable housing units. Homes are expected to be delivered in 2029-2030. The post Shopoff Secures Approval for Buena Park Residential Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Shopoff Realty secured unanimous Buena Park approval for 13.76-acre residential project on 370K SF industrial site
231 townhomes/duplexes + 50 senior affordable units; delivery 2029–2030; Amway leaseback expires end-2026
Industrial-to-residential conversion addresses Orange County's first-time homebuyer and senior housing shortage
stories.summary: Shopoff Realty Investments secured unanimous city council approval in Buena Park for a 13.76-acre residential development at 5600 Beach Boulevard, currently occupied by Amway Corporation under a sale-leaseback expiring end-2026. The project will deliver 231 three-story townhomes and duplex units plus 50 for-rent senior affordable units across four floor plans, with homes expected in 2029–2030.
stories.impact: Significant for Orange County multifamily supply and market position: 231 for-sale townhomes plus 50 affordable rental units represent net addition to Orange County's housing stock and signal municipal appetite for residential conversion of industrial sites. The 2029–2030 delivery timeline aligns with expected Amway lease expiration, reducing permitting/entitlement risk. This precedent validates industrial-to-residential conversions in Orange County and may lower entitlement uncertainty for similar projects in the submarket, accelerating development timelines and improving capital availability for residential plays in transitional industrial zones.

stories.title: Matawan Retail Trades to Private Investor for $15M
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of Park Plaza, a retail center in Matawan, NJ. The asset sold for $14.67 million. “Park Plaza attracted significant investor interest due to its diverse tenant mix, strong visibility and strategic location within one of Monmouth County’s most established retail corridors,” said Seth Goldberg, associate director investments in Marcus & Millichap’s New Jersey office. “Well-positioned neighborhood shopping centers with durable cash flow continue to be highly sought after, and this transaction reflects the sustained demand for quality retail assets in New Jersey.” Goldberg, Brent Hyldahl and Alan Cafiero of Marcus & Millichap marketed the property for the seller and procured the buyer, both private investors from New Jersey. Located at 343-351 State Rte. 34, the retail center sits on a 5.86-acre lot totaling 61,750 square feet. It was built in 1986 and contains 20 suites. The rent roll features a diverse mix of dining, lifestyle, retail and service-oriented tenants, including a Dunkin’ with a drive-thru. The post Matawan Retail Trades to Private Investor for $15M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Park Plaza, Matawan NJ retail center trades for $14.67M; 61,750 SF, 20 suites on 5.86 acres
Built 1986; diverse tenant mix (Dunkin', dining, lifestyle, service); located on Route 34 corridor
Marcus & Millichap cites strong investor demand for neighborhood shopping centers with durable cash flow
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of Park Plaza, a 61,750-square-foot retail center in Matawan, New Jersey, for $14.67 million. The 1986-built asset sits on a 5.86-acre lot with 20 retail suites featuring a diverse tenant mix including a Dunkin' drive-thru, dining, lifestyle, and service tenants. Both buyer and seller were New Jersey-based private investors.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Sustained retail investor demand in Monmouth County may indicate neighborhood resilience and stable foot traffic patterns, but does not materially affect residential supply, demand drivers, or capital deployment for apartment development in the region.

stories.title: Longfellow Sells Hatch Life Sciences Building in LIC for $87M
stories.excerpt: Life sciences developer Longfellow Real Estate Partners has parted with its first-ever New York City project at a discount. Longfellow’s Hatch Life Sciences Building, located at 43-10 23 Street in Long Island City, Queens, has sold for $86.9 million, according to city records filed Friday. Pearl Realty Management’s Jack Guttman signed for the buyer, under the entity 4310 23 St. A representative of Pearl Realty Management did not respond to requests for comment. Longfellow purchased the existing building at 43-10 23 Street in 2021 alongside its partner, Steven Orbuch’s Sculptor Real Estate, for $92.5 million. Longfellow, led by CEO and co-founder Adam Sichol, planned to invest another $120 million into turning the former parachute manufacturing plant into a mix of life sciences labs and offices. Construction had all but wrapped up when Commercial Observer visited in 2024. The final product spanned over 208,000 square feet across seven floors, including prebuilt lab suites, modular research space and flexible office areas. Longfellow and Sculptor did not respond immediately to requests for comment on the sale. While Guttman’s plans for the purchase remain unclear, the landlord appears to be active in the Long Island City market. Recent purchases include the Standard Motors Product Building at 37-18 Northern Boulevard for $42 million and BrightSpire Capital‘s office building at 21-02 49th Avenue for $28 million. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Longfellow Real Estate sold Hatch Life Sciences Building, Long Island City for $86.9M; purchased 2021 for $92.5M
208K SF adaptive-reuse project (208K SF, 7 floors); originally $120M capex; sold at $3.6M loss after completion
Life sciences market weakness or overbuilding in Queens signals potential cap-rate compression or demand softness in specialized real estate
stories.summary: Longfellow Real Estate Partners exited its first New York City project, the Hatch Life Sciences Building at 43-10 23 Street in Long Island City, Queens, for $86.9 million—a $5.6 million loss from its 2021 purchase price of $92.5 million (plus ~$120M planned capex). The 208,000-square-foot adaptive-reuse project across seven floors includes prebuilt lab suites, modular research space, and flexible office. Pearl Realty Management purchased through entity 4310 23 St.
stories.impact: Signal of life sciences market weakness or overbuilding risk in Long Island City/Queens. The below-cost-basis exit—despite completion of $120M+ capital investment—suggests either demand softness for lab/specialized office space in the submarket, cap-rate compression on yields, or broader portfolio/capital redeployment pressures. Multifamily developers should monitor competing supply and pricing power in Long Island City office/lab conversions, which may canibalize residential demand or inflate land prices in the neighborhood. A pivot to residential in Queens mixed-use zones may encounter lower cap rates or slower absorption if office/lab occupancy remains challenged.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Buys Two Miami Affordable Housing Rentals
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has acquired two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from the Gatehouse Group, paying a combined $63.8 million, property records show. In the largest deal, the investor paid $34 million for the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments in the Naranja neighborhood, near the southern end of the county. Built in 2011, the 4.8-acre asset houses 20 three-story buildings at 25881 Southwest 143rd Court, just west of the South Dixie Highway. The sale breaks down to roughly $226,660 per unit. CBRE Capital Partners provided a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan. Across the county in Miami’s Little River neighborhood, Starwood paid $29.75 million for the 160-unit Lafayette Square complex. The 19-story building sits on a 1.2-acre site, a block west from Northeast Second Avenue at 150 Northeast 79th Street. The deal equates to about $185,900 per apartment. The Gatehouse Group appears to have retained ownership of the adjacent 136-unit property. The Mansfield, Mass.-based firm developed both the Lafayette Square and Magnolia Landing Apartments, completing the former in 2008 and the latter in 2011. Representatives for Starwood and Gatehouse Group did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management acquired two Miami-Dade affordable rental properties from Gatehouse Group for $63.8M combined
Magnolia Landing (150 units, Naranja) $34M; Lafayette Square (160 units, Little River) $29.75M; total ~311 units
Freddie Mac loan ($23.8M) on Magnolia; strategic REIT acquisition in supply-constrained Miami affordable market
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management acquired two affordable rental properties in Miami-Dade County from Gatehouse Group for a combined $63.8 million. Magnolia Landing in Naranja (150 units, 2011-built, 4.8 acres, 20 three-story buildings) sold for $34 million ($226,660/unit), with a $23.8M Freddie Mac loan. Lafayette Square in Little River (160 units, 19-story, 1.2 acres) sold for $29.75 million ($185,900/unit).
stories.impact: Strategic signal for Miami affordable housing market: a major institutional investor (Starwood) acquiring ~311 units in two separate affordable rental assets signals strong capital appetite and low-debt-service risk perception in Miami-Dade's affordable housing sector. The sub-$230K/unit pricing and Freddie Mac financing availability indicate favorable cost-of-capital conditions for stabilized affordable multifamily in the metro. Developers should interpret this as a green light for affordable acquisition/development in high-growth Miami-Dade neighborhoods (Naranja, Little River); watch for follow-on acquisitions and potential cap-rate compression as institutional capital competes for limited affordable supply.

stories.title: Ad Agency Doubles Office HQ Space in Move to Hackman Campus in L.A.
stories.excerpt: An international advertising agency is more than doubling its office footprint with a new headquarters lease in El Segundo, Calif. Innocean USA signed the 101,000-square-foot deal at Hackman Capital Partners’ creative office campus in the small enclave just south of Los Angeles International Airport. The agency will relocate nearly 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach after construction on its new space concludes in 2027, according to JLL, which represented the tenant. The company reportedly will use part of the space as a production facility for commercials and other content. Terms of the lease were not disclosed. “This move is about creating the right environment for our next chapter,” Innocean USA CEO Steve Jun said in a statement. “This is an investment in our people, our clients, and the future we’re building together.” The complex, named after its address at 888 Douglas Street, includes four buildings totaling 550,000 square feet over 30 acres. Hackman acquired the former Northrop Grumman aerospace manufacturing complex in 2016, and invested about $100 million converting it into the creative office. Other major occupiers at the property have included L’Oréal USA, which signed for more than 100,000 square feet in 2021, and Beyond Meat, which originally leased 280,000 square feet for its headquarters. Aerospace and defense companies have also returned to L.A.’s South Bay, and helped bolster leasing at the El Segundo campus. Hypersonic aircraft developer Hermeus signed for 62,552 square feet earlier this year, while Varda Space Industries expanded to 54,749 square feet in 2025. Innocean USA is the U.S. arm of Innocean Worldwide, which was created by Hyundai Motor Group. JLL’s Jason Fine, Jeff Ingham and Mitch Lundquist represented Innocean, while Hackman was represented in-house. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Innocean USA signs 101K SF HQ lease at Hackman's 888 Douglas, El Segundo; relocates ~600 from Huntington Beach
Deal mirrors Article 2; 2027 delivery; tenant doubles footprint, adds production facility for content/commercials
CEO: move signals investment in people and clients; creative campus attracts talent and production infrastructure
stories.summary: Innocean USA signed a 101,000-square-foot headquarters lease at Hackman Capital Partners' 888 Douglas creative office campus in El Segundo, relocating nearly 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach. The agency will occupy the space after construction in 2027 and use part of the facility as a production hub for commercials and content. JLL represented the tenant.
stories.impact: Duplicate of Article 2 with additional detail on production-facility use. Reinforces South Los Angeles (El Segundo/LAX corridor) as emerging creative-economy and media-production hub, with downstream implications for nearby residential markets (Manhattan Beach, Torrance, Hermosa Beach, Inglewood). Production facilities and associated creative employment typically draw higher-wage workers and support premium rental housing demand. Monitor apartment rent growth and occupancy in 3–5 mile radius of 888 Douglas over 2027–2029 as workforce stabilizes; expect stronger demand and rent-growth potential vs. Orange County comparables.

stories.title: Attorney James Allen Joins Camber Property Group as Senior Counsel
stories.excerpt: Camber Property Group has onboarded a new general counsel for its affordable housing and community development transactions, Commercial Observer has learned. James Allen has decamped from real estate law firm Hirschen Singer & Epstein and started the new role this week assisting Camber with affordable housing projects in New York state and the New York tri-state region, according to the development firm. “One trend I am seeing is that, in their efforts to solve the ongoing housing affordability crisis, more developers are starting to expand both the types of projects that they participate in and their geographic footprint,” Allen said in a statement. “Camber is always thinking creatively about both, but they present unique challenges.” Allen was previously an associate for four years at Nixon Peabody and a senior staff attorney for the New York Court of Appeals. The Brooklyn Law School graduate also pens articles about housing equity and affordability while serving on the board of the New York Housing Conference’s Rising Leaders Network and the New York City Bar Association’s Housing & Urban Development Committee. Hirschen Singer & Epstein did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “I feel lucky to have the chance to expand upon that and work with many of the legal partners that I have learned from over the years, while Camber solidifies its New York presence and intentionally expands its footprint to other regions,” Allen said. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: James Allen joins Camber Property Group as senior counsel for affordable housing/community development in NY tri-state
Previously at Hirschen Singer & Epstein law firm; former Nixon Peabody, NY Court of Appeals staff attorney
Hire signals Camber expansion in affordable multifamily and geographic footprint beyond core market
stories.summary: Camber Property Group has hired attorney James Allen as senior general counsel for affordable housing and community development transactions, focusing on New York State and the tri-state region. Allen previously worked at real estate law firm Hirschen Singer & Epstein and held roles at Nixon Peabody and the New York Court of Appeals. He is a board member of the New York Housing Conference and NYC Bar Association's Housing & Development committee.
stories.impact: Organizational signal that Camber is scaling affordable housing development operations and expanding geographic reach across the tri-state region. The hire suggests anticipation of larger, more complex transactional volume in affordable multifamily—likely driven by tax-credit, low-income housing preservation, and community development programs. Monitor Camber's pipeline announcements in NY, NJ, CT for affordable development acceleration; this legal infrastructure hire typically precedes capital deployment and new project launches. May indicate available financing or investor appetite for affordable multifamily in secondary NY markets.
